context_requirements: Expression of ACHE and/or butyrylcholinesterase (BCHE) so that acetylcholine can accumulate
Functional nicotinic or muscarinic acetylcholine receptors (CHRN subunits, CHRM) to transduce the cholinergic signal
An intact cholinergic autocrine/paracrine loop; non-neuronal cells with low ACh synthesis or receptor expression will respond weakly
For oxidative-stress and apoptosis-related secondary effects, a stress-responsive (e.g. TP53-competent) background may be needed
falsifiers: No consistent change in any landmark gene at 6 h or 24 h across the nine lines at 10 micromolar
Changes that are equally strong in lines lacking ACHE/BCHE and CHRN expression as in expressing lines
A response dominated by generic proliferation/cell-cycle genes with no cholinergic or immediate-early signature
Dose-response or time-course showing no transcriptional effect at 10 micromolar despite measurable ACHE inhibition

evidence.supports: AChE inhibitors can act through non-cholinergic (NMDA-receptor-linked ERK/p38) pathways, so transcriptional effects may be indirect and cell-type dependent
Donepezil reduces oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, necroptosis and apoptosis in vivo, supporting late oxidative-stress/apoptosis signatures
Donepezil activates HIF-1alpha/VEGF and angiogenic signalling via cholinergic (alpha7 nAChR) pathways, indicating receptor-dependent transcriptional consequences
AChE inhibition by soman produces a time-dependent hippocampal gene-expression response, supporting a measurable but delayed transcriptional program
AChE inhibitors protect PC12 cells from H2O2-induced apoptosis and ROS, supporting oxidative-stress-related secondary responses
